claims.text: The starting material consists of sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles produced by pulsed laser deposition on a silicon nitride membrane.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles have a disordered FCC structure.
The initial nanoparticles have elliptical or icosahedral morphology.
Au and Cu are the low-surface-energy elements in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Surface-energy minimization drives Au and Cu to segregate to the nanoparticle surface.
Au/Cu surface segregation creates a steep chemical-potential gradient.
The chemical-potential gradient overrides the sluggish-diffusion effect associated with high configurational entropy.
The local multicomponent environment lowers the surface-diffusion barriers of Au and Cu.
Element-dependent diffusion can cause preferential outward transport and near-surface depletion in multicomponent alloys.
Increasing temperature can increase the diffusivity of a preferentially mobile element and maintain its transport to an interface.
Rapid surface diffusion is followed by evaporation or sublimation of Au and Cu.
Au/Cu mass loss causes reshaping from elliptical or icosahedral particles to spherical particles.
The dominant Au/Cu segregation and evaporation regime begins between 600 °C and 800 °C for sub-5 nm particles.
Above the critical temperature, Au/Cu surface segregation and evaporation become faster than bulk diffusion.
Initially icosahedral particles reshape faster than truncated octahedra because their vertices give them a higher surface-energy density.
Heating produces a smaller core depleted in Au and Cu and enriched in Co, Cr, Ni, and Pt.
Surface-energy terms dominate the Gibbs free energy only for particles smaller than 10 nm.
For particles larger than 20 nm, bulk diffusion and entropy stabilization dominate over the proposed surface mechanism.
Sluggish diffusion can hinder growth and promote nanocrystalline microstructures in high-entropy-alloy films.
Independence of Au/Cu loss and reshaping from initial particle shape would falsify surface-energy gradients as the driver.

contradictions.description: The starting alloy contains Au, Co, Cu, Ni, and Pt but no Cr, whereas the predicted final core is described as CoCrNiPt-enriched. Cr cannot become enriched without an unreported Cr source; simple Au/Cu depletion would leave a Co-Ni-Pt-enriched core.

The structural mediator says the surface-energy gradient is induced by Au/Cu segregation, while the mechanism says surface energy drives that segregation. This makes the stated causal ordering circular unless an initial surface-energy gradient independent of segregation is defined.
